title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Withdrawal - Tribunal Leave
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal decides they must mandatorily withdraw from a case because the client is instructing them to act fraudulently. However, the withdrawal occurs on the morning of a heavily scheduled LTB hearing. The adjudicator refuses to grant leave to withdraw. What is the paralegal's position?
options: The paralegal must walk out of the hearing regardless of the adjudicator's ruling.
The paralegal must follow the adjudicator's direction, remain on the record, but must not assist the client in presenting any fraudulent evidence.
The paralegal must remain on the record and execute the client's fraudulent instructions, as tribunal orders trump LSO rules.
The paralegal must report the adjudicator to the police for obstruction of justice.
questions.explain: If a tribunal refuses leave for the representative to withdraw, the paralegal is bound to remain on the record. However, their ethical obligations prevent them from suborning perjury or presenting fraudulent evidence. They must proceed with the case utilizing only the lawful, truthful portions of the evidence.
